root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list_len <= WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN before the secondary-device-type memcpy
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `p2p_copy_client_info()` copies `cli->sec_dev_types` into `dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list`, the derived length `dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list_len` must not exceed `WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN`. Otherwise the copy writes past the fixed 128-byte array into adjacent fields of the same `struct p2p_device` object.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the protected copy with `dev->info.wps_sec_dev_type_list_len = 152` while `WPS_SEC_DEV_TYPE_MAX_LEN = 128`. The fixed original still executes the same copy after clamping the length to 128, so the missing bound is genuinely satisfied on the fixed side.

nodes.state: Immediately after the secondary-device-type `os_memcpy`, the adjacent `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[0]` slot no longer matches its pre-copy value, proving the overflowing copy mutated the pointer field inside the same `struct p2p_device` object.
On the first vendor-extension cleanup iteration (`i == 0`), `p2p_device_free()` passes `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[i]` to `wpabuf_free()`.
`wpabuf_free()` reaches the source-level sink `if (buf->flags & WPABUF_FLAG_EXT_DATA)` with the same pointer that came from the corrupted vendor-extension slot.

edges.relation: Across the same `p2p_copy_client_info()` copy site, violating the missing length bound lets the secondary-device-type `os_memcpy` change adjacent `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[0]` from its pre-copy value to a different post-copy value.
The post-copy value stored in `dev->info.wps_vendor_ext[0]` is retained in the same `struct p2p_device` object until teardown and becomes the first `wpabuf_free()` argument in `p2p_device_free()`.
The same first-iteration vendor-extension pointer that `p2p_device_free()` passes to `wpabuf_free()` becomes the callee's `buf` parameter at the later `buf->flags` read sink.
